_comment: SPARK — S166 P3 REV 2: the SIX TIER-9 BOSS STRUCTURES, three states each = 18 pieces.
⛔ REV 1 WAS REJECTED BY THE OWNER ON TWO COUNTS, AND THE FIRST IS A PROCESS BUG, NOT A TASTE
CALL. He wrote: *"towers and their states are not consistent (look at the the zombie building
and youll see the second state looks like a shack while the first one looks like a house)"*.
⭐ THE CAUSE: REV 1 WROTE THREE INDEPENDENT TEXT PROMPTS PER RACE. A text description of a
building yields *a* building, not *THAT* building — so the model drew three different structures
and called them three states. The naga set drifted the same way (intact = a coral-pillared
rampart, damaged = a stone cistern in three-quarter view) and only escaped the report because
the owner liked the first one.
⭐ THE FIX IS THE MECHANISM THIS SCRIPT ALREADY HAS, AND ITS OWN DOCBLOCK ARGUES FOR IT:
`refImages` exists for *"an IDENTITY constraint, not a style one... A text description of a
burlap sack yields *a* burlap sack; the actual pixels of the owner's own hanging sacks yield THAT
sack."* So every DAMAGED and DESTROYED entry below carries its own INTACT png as a reference
image and is written as an instruction ABOUT that image. Generate the intacts FIRST.
⛔ THE SECOND REJECTION WAS THE CONCEPTS, and the owner replaced five of six by hand:
· Vlad      — a ROYAL VAMPIRE COFFIN (*"obv"*), not a gothic spire.
· Whopper   — a NASTY BACTA TANK / POD, not a slaughterhouse shed.
· Warlord   — a WARLORD HUT/TENT, *"but cooler and scarier looking"*, not a stone blockhouse.
· Archdemon — a CRACK IN THE FLOOR / OPENING IN THE GROUND, *"straight out of hell"*, not a
freestanding arch.
· Pharaoh   — a TOMB that is *"cooler and more consistent... like CURSED"*, not a clean pyramid.
· Kraken    — KEPT. *"the kraken one you generated looks good"*. The intact png is unchanged
and is now the reference its own two damaged states are drawn from.
⭐ AND THE THROUGH-LINE HE GAVE: *"they all need to be more distinct and appropriate for the
race"*. Each structure is now the place ITS boss came out of — a coffin for the lord, a tank for
the thing that was grown, a tent for the warlord who travels, a fissure for the thing from below.
That is a stronger identity rule than 'a tower in the race's colours', which is what REV 1 had.
⚠ NEXT SESSION: the per-race destroy CINEMATIC, deferred by the owner. The DESTROYED state below
is the still END-STATE that cinematic must land on, so it is drawn as settled wreckage.
_gravity: ⛔ GRAVITY. Every broken, snapped or detached piece must have COME TO REST ON THE GROUND at the
base of the structure — lying flat, leaning against it, or half-buried in its own rubble.
Nothing detached may float, hang in mid-air, dangle unsupported or sit at a mid-fall angle.
sharedStyle: Cartoon vector game-asset illustration in a bold black ink outline style with flat cel shading
and a few crisp highlight streaks — the drawing language of a hand-inked tabletop game piece, at
BOSS weight: heavier outlines, deeper shadow, more material detail than an ordinary tower.
An ORIGINAL design — not resembling any existing franchise, film or game.
FULL COLOUR with real material variety: deeper cooler shades of the main hue for shadow, lighter
tints for lit faces, visible texture in the stone, timber, bone, hide, glass or iron, and one or
two supporting materials (dark iron, weathered timber, dull bronze, tarnished chain) that are NOT
the main hue.
⛔ NEVER a single flat fill: it must read as a real object made of materials, not a silhouette.
⛔ NOTHING MAY BE WHITE OR NEAR-WHITE. Every light tone must carry a visible colour cast a painter
would name — bone-yellow, dull ochre, sea-green, warm tan, steel-blue, cold lavender-grey. Even
the brightest highlight stays clearly tinted. The background is the only white in the image.
⛔ GRAVITY. Every broken or detached piece must have COME TO REST ON THE GROUND at the base —
lying flat, leaning, or half-buried in its own rubble. Nothing floats or hangs at a mid-fall angle.
Symmetrical straight-on FRONT ELEVATION, no perspective, no three-quarter view, no tilt.
THE WHOLE STRUCTURE FROM ITS BASE TO ITS VERY TOP is inside the frame with clear empty margin
above it — nothing cropped by any edge.
⛔ NO GROUND SHADOW, no cast shadow, no ground plane, no base platform, no scenery. The lowest ink
in the image must be part of the structure itself or its own fallen rubble.
Centered on a plain pure white background.
No text, no logo, no border, no frame, no white outline around the silhouette, no die-cut sticker
edge, no drop-shadow, no background scenery, no characters.

characters.name: t9-vampires-intact
characters._race: vampires — crimson — VLAD'S COFFIN (owner: 'a royal vampire coffin - obv')
characters.prompt: A royal vampire's coffin standing UPRIGHT on a low stepped bier, shown complete from the base of the bier to the top of the lid with clear empty margin above. A tall tapered hexagonal casket of near-black timber, its whole face carved in deep gothic relief and framed by heavy blackened-iron strapwork with big rivets and clawed corner mounts. Set into the centre of the lid is a large crimson stained-glass panel shaped like a pointed arch, glowing dark red from within, with a tarnished bronze bat-wing crest above it and a heraldic clasp of dull bronze holding the lid shut. Deep oxblood velvet padding shows in the seam along the lid's edge. The bier is dark violet-grey stone with two carved bat gargoyles at its front corners. Rich, ornate and funereal — a nobleman's casket, not a plain box.

characters.name: t9-vampires-damaged
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same upright coffin, same silhouette, same hexagonal lid, same iron strapwork, same crimson arch panel, same bier, same colours and materials, same position in the frame — but now BATTERED AND BREACHED. The bronze clasp is snapped and the lid has split down its length, gaping open along a jagged crack; one corner of the lid has broken away and rests on the bier step below. The crimson glass panel is shattered, its glow guttering and uneven through the broken shards still in the frame. Two iron straps are torn loose and bent back, and one bat gargoyle has broken off the bier and lies on its side on the ground at the base. Long claw-gouges and soot streaks mark the timber. Same building, hurt — not a different coffin.

characters.name: t9-vampires-destroyed
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same coffin, same materials, same palette, same bier — but now DESTROYED AND SETTLED. The casket has come down off the bier and lies broken open on the ground: the tapered hull is split in half lengthwise, the lid is off entirely and lies flat beside it, and the interior oxblood velvet lining is torn and exposed. The crimson glass panel is gone, only jagged dark shards remain in a bent bronze frame lying among the wreckage; there is no glow left, just a dull ember in the deepest gap. Snapped iron strapwork, rivets and both broken gargoyles lie scattered flat across the rubble. Only the low stepped stone bier still stands, cracked and empty. Same building, finished. Every piece rests on the ground.

characters.name: t9-nagas-damaged
characters._race: nagas — cyan — KEPT DESIGN (owner approved the intact)
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same abyssal pit, same circular teal stone rampart, same four inward-leaning coral pillars, same barnacles, same chain and netting, same STRAIGHT-ON FRONT ELEVATION, same colours and proportions, same position in the frame — but now BATTERED. Two of the four coral pillars are snapped mid-length and their broken upper halves lie across the rampart and on the ground at the base. A section of the stone rim has collapsed inward, spilling teal blocks and coral fragments. The bronze chain hangs slack and broken with one end coiled on the ground, and the netting is torn away down one side. The cyan glow rising from the pit is uneven and guttering, and the algae is scorched dark in patches. Same structure, hurt — not a different pit, and NOT a three-quarter view.

characters.name: t9-nagas-destroyed
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same abyssal pit, same teal stone, same coral, same chain, same STRAIGHT-ON FRONT ELEVATION, same position in the frame — but now DESTROYED AND SETTLED. The rampart is broken down to a low uneven ring of teal blocks and the central opening is choked with collapsed rubble. All four coral pillars are down, snapped into lengths that lie flat across the ruin and on the ground around it. Broken bronze chain lies in loose coils among the blocks and the netting is a torn heap. Dead coral and barnacles scatter the debris. The cyan glow is gone — only a faint sickly green seep remains in the deepest gap. Same structure, finished. Every piece rests on the ground.

characters.name: t9-mummies-intact
characters._race: mummies — yellow — THE CURSED TOMB (owner: 'cooler and more consistent... like cursed')
characters.prompt: A cursed pharaoh's tomb entrance, shown complete from its base to its very top with clear empty margin above. A broad squat mastaba of dark bronze-brown sandstone with battered sloping sides, far heavier and more sinister than a clean pyramid. Its face is dominated by a tall SEALED false door of black granite banded in tarnished gold, chained shut across the middle with heavy corroded bronze chain and a great cracked wax seal. Deep-carved hieroglyph bands run across the face, and the carvings glow with a sickly amber curse-light that bleeds out of the grooves. Two towering jackal-headed sentinel statues of black stone and dull gold flank the door, heads bowed inward. Drifted ochre sand banks against the base and pours in thin streams from the cracks. Yellow accents: the curse-glow in the carvings and the gold banding. Sealed, malevolent and waiting.

characters.name: t9-mummies-damaged
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same squat mastaba, same sloping sides, same black granite false door, same gold banding, same chains and seal, same two jackal sentinels, same colours and proportions, same position in the frame — but now BATTERED AND BREACHED. The wax seal is shattered and the bronze chains have snapped, their loose ends lying coiled on the sand; the false door has been forced inward and hangs crooked, opening a black gap. A corner of the mastaba's upper edge has caved in, spilling bronze-brown blocks down the slope to the ground. One jackal sentinel has toppled and lies on its side at the foot of the door, the other is cracked through the shoulder. The amber curse-light burns brighter and wilder through the widened cracks, and sand pours freely. Same tomb, hurt.

characters.name: t9-mummies-destroyed
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same mastaba, same materials, same palette, same jackal sentinels — but now DESTROYED AND SETTLED. Only the lowest third of the tomb remains, a broad flattened stump of bronze-brown sandstone with a ragged broken top. The upper mass has come down and lies heaped around it. The black granite false door lies flat on the ground, cracked in two, its gold banding buckled and the broken chain strewn across it. Both jackal sentinels are down and broken, one head lying separate among the blocks. Hieroglyph fragments and loose gold inlay scatter the rubble; the entrance is collapsed and choked with sand. The amber curse-light is out — only a dull glimmer deep in the fallen stones. Same tomb, finished. Every piece rests on the ground.

characters.name: t9-zombies-intact
characters._race: zombies — green — THE GROWTH POD (owner: 'a nasty bacta tank or pod')
characters.prompt: A filthy flesh-growing tank, shown complete from its base to its very top with clear empty margin above. A tall heavy cylindrical vat of thick greenish glass held in a riveted frame of rusted dark iron, standing on a squat corroded iron base. The glass is filmed with grime and streaked with dried residue. Inside, foul luminous green fluid churns with drifting sediment, and the dim bloated silhouette of a huge malformed body hangs suspended in it, hunched, its outline blurred by the murk. Thick ribbed rubber hoses and corroded copper piping run from the base up into the frame; a heavy iron collar with pressure valves and a cracked gauge caps the top. Rust runs from every rivet and green sludge crusts the base seams. Green accents: the luminous fluid and sickly light spilling from it. Industrial, filthy and wrong.

characters.name: t9-zombies-damaged
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY - same cylindrical glass tank, same rusted iron frame and rivets, same base, same hoses and copper piping, same top collar and gauge, same colours and proportions, same position in the frame - but now SLIGHTLY CRACKED AND OOZING. ⚠ THIS IS A LIGHT WOUND, NOT A WRECK. The tank is still standing, still full and still sealed apart from the damage described here. A single jagged crack runs down one side of the glass in a spidering star pattern; luminous green fluid weeps steadily from it in thick runs down the outside of the tank and puddles in a small pool at the base. The fluid level inside is still HIGH and the bloated body is STILL SUSPENDED in the murk, unchanged. One hose fitting has sprung a leak and drips. The gauge glass is cracked across its face. Everything else - the frame, the collar, both hoses, the base - is intact and in place. Same tank, wounded and leaking, not broken.
characters._owner_note: S166 REV 2b - owner: "second state of the pod is cracked slightly and oozing and third is completely destroyed". REV 2a over-destroyed this state: it blew out a whole glass panel, dropped the fluid level and REMOVED THE BODY, which left almost nothing for the destroyed state to escalate to. Softened to a hairline breach with the body still suspended, so the three states read as a real progression: sealed -> weeping -> gone.

characters.name: t9-zombies-destroyed
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same tank, same iron frame, same palette and materials — but now DESTROYED AND SETTLED. The glass cylinder is almost entirely gone, leaving a jagged collar of green shards standing in the twisted iron frame; the frame itself is buckled and leans, one strut snapped and lying flat on the ground. The top collar and its gauge have come off and lie among the debris. Every hose is torn free and lies limp and flat. A wide spreading pool of dull green sludge has run out across the ground and soaked into the wreckage, thick with glass fragments. Only the corroded iron base still stands, split and empty. The luminous glow is nearly out — a dim sickly shine in the pool. Same tank, finished. Every piece rests on the ground.

characters.name: t9-orcs-intact
characters._race: orcs — orange — THE WAR TENT (owner: 'a warlord hut/tent but cooler and scarier')
characters.prompt: An orc warlord's war-tent, shown complete from its base to its very top with clear empty margin above. A broad heavy hide tent of dark umber and olive beast-skins stitched together with thick leather cord, stretched over a frame of huge curved bone ribs and blackened timber poles that cross above the peak and jut out like horns. The entrance is a wide flap of dark hide pinned back by two iron-shod stakes, showing a black interior with a low orange fire-glow. Enormous tusks flank the doorway. Trophy poles rise at each side hung with cracked skulls, tarnished bronze rings and captured blades, and a ragged battle-banner of dark leather hangs from the crossed peak poles. Heavy stones and iron pegs weigh the hem down all round. Orange accents: the fire-glow at the entrance and rust-orange banding on the iron. Squat, wide, brutal and unmistakably a warlord's seat.

characters.name: t9-orcs-damaged
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same hide war-tent, same bone-rib frame, same crossed horn poles, same entrance and tusks, same trophy poles and banner, same colours and proportions, same position in the frame — but now BATTERED. The hide is slashed open in two long rents down one side, the flaps hanging inward and showing the bone ribs behind. One of the crossed peak poles is snapped and its broken upper length has come down and lies across the tent roof and onto the ground. The banner is torn nearly in half. One trophy pole has toppled and lies flat, its skulls scattered on the ground at the base. Two hem stones are dislodged and the hide has pulled free there, sagging. The entrance fire-glow burns brighter through the new rents. Same tent, hurt.

characters.name: t9-orcs-destroyed
characters.prompt: Redraw the structure in the reference image EXACTLY — same tent, same hides, same bone ribs, same palette — but now DESTROYED AND SETTLED. The tent has collapsed: the hide covering has come down entirely and lies flat and crumpled across the ground in a low heap, torn through in several places. Two bone ribs still stand, snapped and leaning, the rest are down and lie flat among the hides. Both crossed peak poles have fallen and lie full length on the ground. Both trophy poles are down, skulls and bent blades strewn through the wreckage; the banner lies trampled and half-buried. The hem stones sit in a scattered ring around the flattened heap. Only a dull ember glow remains where the entrance fire was. Same tent, finished. Every piece rests on the ground.

characters.name: t9-demons-intact
characters._race: demons — magenta — THE HELLMOUTH (owner: 'a crack in the floor/opening in the ground - straight out of hell')
characters.prompt: A hellmouth torn open in the ground, shown complete with clear empty margin above it — a WIDE LOW GROUND FEATURE, not a tower. A jagged fissure splits a raised broken slab of charred black basalt, the rock heaved upward around the gap into a low ragged rim like torn skin, the slabs tilted and cracked apart. The fissure itself is a deep vertical wound filled with searing magenta hellfire, its light throwing hot magenta up the inner faces of the broken rock. Curved black horns of stone jut upward from the rim on both sides, and fused fragments of blackened iron armour and snapped chain are embedded in the cooling crust. Fine cracks radiate outward across the slab, glowing magenta along their length. Embers rise from the gap. The whole feature is wider than it is tall and its lowest ink is the broken rock itself. Vicious, raw and freshly torn open.

characters.name: t9-demons-damaged
characters.prompt: Redraw the feature in the reference image EXACTLY - same hellmouth, same heaved basalt rim, same stone horns, same embedded iron, same radiating cracks, same wide low proportions, same position in the frame - but now HALF CLOSED. ⚠ THIS FEATURE DOES NOT BREAK APART, IT SHUTS: the ground is grinding back together. The fissure has squeezed to roughly half its width, its two rock lips pushed toward each other with fresh rubble wedged and crushed between them along its length. The magenta hellfire is reduced to a narrow ragged ribbon deep in the remaining gap, far dimmer, with only a few embers left. Two stone horns have slumped inward and lean over the closing gap. About half the radiating cracks have gone dark and cooled to grey. The rim is still whole - nothing has shattered or scattered. Same feature, closing.
characters._owner_note: S166 REV 2b - owner: "for hellmouth is the opposite - it closes as it gets destroyed". The other five structures BREAK APART across their states; this one SHUTS. Worth stating because it inverts the whole set's logic: for the hellmouth, 'more damaged' means LESS opening and LESS fire, and its destroyed state is the tidiest image of the six rather than the most scattered.

characters.name: t9-demons-destroyed
characters.parameters_note: the END-STATE the destroy cinematic must land on
characters.prompt: Redraw the feature in the reference image EXACTLY - same basalt slab, same rim, same palette, same wide low proportions, same position in the frame - but now COMPLETELY CLOSED AND COLD. ⚠ THE OPENING IS GONE: the two rock lips have ground fully shut, leaving only a healed seam of fused dark stone where the fissure was, like a scar. NO gap, NO opening, and NO fire of any kind - not one ember. Every radiating crack is dark, cooled to grey and choked with grey ash. The heaved rim has settled back down almost flush with the slab, and the stone horns have slumped and fused into low worn stumps. Embedded iron fragments are half-swallowed by the cooled rock. The whole feature is grey, inert and quiet - the tidiest of the set, because this one closes rather than shatters. Same feature, sealed.
characters._owner_note: S166 REV 2b - the END of the owner's inverted progression: fully shut. Deliberately the calmest image in the set - a sealed scar, not a debris field.
